draft.why_angle: The cited guides list the EZ1-LV and HiFlow Pro LV ratings and certificates but mark input limits as 'not stated' and never say which panel suits which inverter. This page sets out each maker's panel size range and input current and voltage limits side by side, plus APsystems' own rule that the EZ1 runs from panels only (never a battery) and goes on a non-backup outlet.
must: two 315–660 W panels at up to 18 A each

page.title: Best Plug-In Solar Inverter (2026): Which Panels Each One Can Take
page.h1: Best plug-in solar inverter: match the panels to the inputs
page.desc: The APsystems EZ1-LV takes two 315–660 W panels on one 900 VA plug-in microinverter. Hoymiles HiFlow Pro LV models take one each. Input limits and prices compared.
page.answer: Short answer. The best plug in solar inverter for a US balcony is the APsystems EZ1-LV: one 900 VA microinverter takes two 315–660 W panels at up to 18 A each, where a Hoymiles HiFlow Pro LV takes one panel at 14–16 A. Feed it from panels, not a battery, through a non-backup wall outlet.
page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Cost per VA of output: EZ1-LV $325 ÷ 900 VA = $0.361; HMS-420 $160.42 ÷ 420 VA = $0.382; HMS-391 $169 ÷ 391 VA = $0.432; HMS-360 $159 ÷ 360 VA = $0.442.
  • Two panels: one EZ1-LV gives 900 VA for $325. Two HMS-420s give 840 VA for $320.84 (2 × $160.42). Two HMS-391s give 782 VA for $338 (2 × $169).
  • Two 450 W panels: 2 × 450 W = 900 W DC, which matches the EZ1-LV's 900 VA. On two HMS-360s each panel is held to 360 VA, so you get 720 VA.
  • Current into the outlet: 900 VA ÷ 120 V = 7.5 A for the EZ1-LV; 420 VA ÷ 120 V = 3.5 A for the HMS-420.
  • Panel current headroom: the EZ1-LV accepts 18 A per input, 4 A more than the 14 A limit on the HMS-360, 391 and 420.

Matching panels to a plug-in solar inverter

A plug-in microinverter only takes panels whose voltage and current stay within its input limits. Check the panel's label: open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay below the inverter's maximum input voltage, and short-circuit current (Isc) must stay within its input current rating.

  • APsystems EZ1-LV: two independent inputs, each rated for 315 W to 660 W+ panels. Operating range is 26–60 V, MPPT tracking runs from 27 V to 45 V, and each input accepts up to 18 A, or 25 A short-circuit. APsystems allows smaller panels if their voltage and current fall within those limits. The example panels APsystems lists have a Voc of about 49 V and an Isc of about 11.5 A. The EZ1-LV is the only EZ1 model sold in the US.
  • Hoymiles HiFlow Pro LV: one panel per unit, so you choose the model to fit the panel. Hoymiles lists a maximum input of 64 V for every model. The input current limit is 14 A on the 360, 391 and 420, 15 A on the 450, and 16 A on the 500. Recommended panel sizes run from 280–470 W+ on the HMS-360 to 400–670 W+ on the HMS-500. Hoymiles allows up to four units per system and lists 1,200 W total output for a four-unit system. It also says the AC plug's residual voltage drops below 15 Vac within 0.16 s of being unplugged.
  • No batteries, no backup outlets: APsystems says the EZ1 must be connected to a PV module and that running it from a battery could make it malfunction and fail. It also says to plug it into a non-backup outlet. The EZ1 shuts down during a grid outage and restarts only after the grid has been stable for five minutes. Don't run it from a portable power station or plug it into one; to charge a power station, connect the panels to the station's own solar input instead.
  • Which circuit: as reported by pluginsolarcheck, the EZ1-LV's CSA UL 3700 certificate requires one of three setups: a dedicated 10 A circuit; a listed bidirectional Class A GFCI on a shared circuit; or a locking plug with a matching permanently installed receptacle. UL notes that combined current from the utility and a plug-in source can exceed the wiring's rating without tripping the breaker. APsystems' video says two EZ1s give 1,800 W on a standard 15 A circuit. That works out to 2 × 7.5 A = 15 A, the breaker's full rating, so follow the certificate, not the video.
  • EcoFlow STREAM Microinverter: on EcoFlow's US page it adds solar input to a STREAM Ultra, raising that system's grid output from 800 W to 1,200 W. EcoFlow sells the system for plug-and-play use in Utah only.

Not recommended

A Hoymiles HMS-360 with a panel above its 470 W+ range. Each HMS-360 is held to 360 VA, so a 500 W panel loses up to 140 W at peak (500 − 360). For panels that size, choose the EZ1-LV, which takes up to 660 W+ per input.
